On September 30, 2023, Francis created Prevost a cardinal with the rank of Cardinal-Deacon and assigned the deaconry of [Santa Monica degli Agostiniani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica_degli_Agostiniani "Santa Monica degli Agostiniani").[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-119) As prefect, he played a critical role in [evaluating and recommending episcopal candidates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appointment_of_Catholic_bishops "Appointment of Catholic bishops") worldwide, increasing his visibility within the church.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-120) These roles elevated his prominence as a papal candidate leading into the conclave.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-NCR_2025-121)[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-122)[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-123) In October 2023, Francis appointed him as a member of seven additional [dicasteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicasteries "Dicasteries"),[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[h\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-124) and also named him to the [Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_the_Vatican_City_State "Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)

On February 6, 2025, Francis promoted Prevost to cardinal-bishop, assigning him as [titular bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titular_bishop "Titular bishop") of the [Suburbicarian Diocese of Albano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburbicarian_Diocese_of_Albano "Suburbicarian Diocese of Albano").[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-125)[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-126)[\[i\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-128) On February 11, he was appointed to the dignity and rank of [Bailiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiff "Bailiff") Grand Cross of Honour and Devotion of the [Order of Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta "Sovereign Military Order of Malta") by [Grand Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Master_of_the_Order_of_St._John_of_Jerusalem "Grand Master of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem") Fra' [John Dunlap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_T._Dunlap "John T. Dunlap").[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-129)

Written works before the papacy and theology of leadership
----------------------------------------------------------

Given his focus on mission, the writings of Prevost before his election were few.[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-130)[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-131) When he was global head of the Augustinians, the _Rule and Constitutions of the Order of Saint Augustine_ was "issued by Authority of the Prior General, Robert F. Prevost" in 2002.[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-132)

Aside from four journal articles published mostly in Augustininan journals, his main work of scholarship is his doctoral dissertation, _The office and authority of the local Prior in the Order of Saint Augustine_, published by the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas in 1987. The work has been noted for its legal precision, Augustinian roots, [postconciliar engagement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council") and historical depth.[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Towell-2025-1-133) Much of the commentary see this work as a window to his "vision of the church" and "theology of leadership."[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Towell-2025-2-134)[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-U-Sydney-135)[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-136)

In his thesis, Prevost sees that authority is received from above, and therefore "the substance of the office of the superior is to obey; to obey the will of God and to put great effort into trying to know it, to formulate it and to specify it for his subjects."[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Towell-2025-1-133) Leadership is based on [Jesus Christ's threefold offices of teaching, sanctifying and governing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threefold_office "Threefold office"), who sanctifies by prayer and builds community by being centered on the Mass, having "the care of the Brothers, 'especially in spiritual matters.'" The prior must help make the sacraments regular and reverent, protecting "each brother's freedom of conscience while promoting 'frequent' confession."[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Towell-2025-2-134)

Based on St. Augustine's concept, Prevost sees authority as a service.[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-137) He says that service means "listening to what the Spirit is saying in His people so that His projects can be carried out freely and willingly. The Prior then is called to listen, so that together they can discern and implement what the Spirit inspires."[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-U-Sydney-135)

Papacy (2025–present)
---------------------

### Election

[![Image 10](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV waving from the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica in his first public appearance

In pre-conclave speculation, Prevost was considered a [dark horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_horse "Dark horse") compared to more prominent _[papabili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papabili "Papabili")_,[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Maddox_&_Gooch_2025-138)[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-139) although he was noted to be an ally of Pope Francis and a possible compromise candidate.[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Maddox_&_Gooch_2025-138)[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-140) His American nationality had been regarded as a potential stumbling block to his candidacy, reflecting unease about enhancing the United States's geopolitical power.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Rocca-2025-11)[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-141) Prevost was well aware of this, explaining to a friend by text message: "I'm an American, I can't be elected".[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) Supporters argued that he represented a "dignified [middle of the road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_media "Via media")".[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Rich_2025-142)

Prevost was elected Pope on May 8, 2025, the second day of the [conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_conclave "Papal conclave"), on the fourth ballot. White smoke appeared from the [Sistine Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel") at 18:07 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") ([UTC+2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%2B2 "UTC+2")), signifying to the public that a Pope had been chosen.[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-143) After accepting his election and adopting his [papal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name"), Leo embraced his fellow cardinals upon exiting the Sistine Chapel. Cardinal [Dominique Mamberti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Mamberti "Dominique Mamberti"), the [cardinal protodeacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_protodeacon "Cardinal protodeacon"), made the traditional [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") proclamation, __[Habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")__, announcing Pope Leo XIV to the public for the first time from the central [loggia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loggia "Loggia") of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica").[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-144)[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Galeazzi_2025-145) According to [Italian law enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Italy "Law enforcement in Italy"), by the time of the _[habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")_ announcement, there were up to 150,000 in the square.[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-146)

Leo appeared wearing the traditional [papal stole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_regalia_and_insignia "Papal regalia and insignia") and [mozzetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozzetta "Mozzetta"),[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-147) vestments [Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") did not wear upon his greeting of the world following his election.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-148)[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Palma_2025-149) His [pectoral cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_cross "Pectoral cross") was one he wore during the conclave, a gift from the Postulator General of the Augustinian Order when he became a cardinal, containing relics from Saint Augustine and his mother [Saint Monica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Monica "Saint Monica"), among others.[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-150) He then delivered his first address to Rome and the world in Italian, advocating for peace and dialogue, expressing gratitude for the legacy of Pope Francis and quoting Saint Augustine; he also greeted his former diocese of Chiclayo, Peru, in Spanish. After the speech, he imparted his first _[Urbi et Orbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbi_et_Orbi "Urbi et Orbi")_ blessing in Latin.[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-151)[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-152)[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-153)

Leo XIV is the first Pope from the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine") and the second Pope from [the Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Americas "The Americas") (after Pope Francis), and is counted as the 267th pope.[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-154)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Kirby_&_Wells_2025-155)[\[j\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-156) He is a [dual citizen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_citizenship "Dual citizenship") of [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") and the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Burga_2025-157)[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-158)[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-159) He is the first American pope,[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-160) in [the sense of being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_/(word/) "American (word)") the first born in the United States.[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-161)[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-162)[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-163) He is the second to be a native English speaker, after the English-born [Adrian IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_IV "Adrian IV") (r. 1154–1159), who would have spoken [Middle English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_English "Middle English").[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-164) Leo is also the first Pope born after [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and during the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), and thus the first to be born in the [Baby Boomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Boomer "Baby Boomer") generation.[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-165)[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-166) While Leo is the first Pope from the Order of Saint Augustine,[\[157\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-167)[\[158\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-168) six previous popes belonged to other orders which follow the [Augustinian Rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_Saint_Augustine "Rule of Saint Augustine"), the last one prior to Leo being [Pope Eugene IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Eugene_IV "Pope Eugene IV") (1431–1447).[\[159\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-169)

### Inauguration

[![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV's first [popemobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popemobile "Popemobile") ride during his inauguration

On May 9, the day after his election, Leo celebrated his first [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_in_the_Catholic_Church "Mass in the Catholic Church") as Pope in the Sistine Chapel before the assembled [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals"). During the Mass, he preached against the lack of faith in the world, and spoke of a church that would act as a "beacon that illuminates the dark nights of this world".[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-170) Media reported that Leo would take up permanent residence in the [papal apartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_apartments "Papal apartments") in the [Apostolic Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace "Apostolic Palace") rather than in the [Domus Sanctae Marthae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae "Domus Sanctae Marthae") where Francis lived.[\[161\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-171)[\[162\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-172)[\[163\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-173)

Leo's [inauguration Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV") was held on May 18 in [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square").[\[164\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-174)[\[165\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Vatican-Inauguration-2025-175)[\[166\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Petrine-176) During the Mass, he received the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") and his [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman") before 12 representatives of the people of God, including cardinals and bishops, who vowed obedience to the new pope.[\[167\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-177) On May 25, he was formally installed as [Bishop of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_of_Rome "Bishop of Rome") in a ceremony at the [Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran").[\[168\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-178)

### Post-election reactions and impact

In [Chiclayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiclayo "Chiclayo"), thousands crowded the city square for a Mass of Thanksgiving following Leo's election. Similar Masses were celebrated all over Peru.[\[169\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-179) In the US, over 30,000 Americans gathered at Chicago's [Rate Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_Field "Rate Field") for a youth-focused celebration with a video message of Leo XIV who urged Catholics to be "beacons of hope".[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-180)

Political leaders sent their congratulations. President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") stated that it is "a Great Honor for our Country", while Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance"), a Catholic, talked about Catholics and other Christians praying "for his successful work leading the Church". The European Council President [António Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa "António Costa") said it was "a moment of hope".[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-181)

### Early acts

On June 5, 2025, Leo nominated Joseph Lin Yuntuan as [auxiliary bishop of Fuzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Archdiocese_of_Fuzhou "Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Fuzhou"), which was approved by Chinese authorities on June 11 as part of a 2018 agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Holy See under Pope Francis.[\[172\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-182) On July 5, Leo appointed French archbishop [Thibault Verny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thibault_Verny "Thibault Verny") to succeed [Seán Patrick O'Malley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%A1n_Patrick_O%27Malley "Seán Patrick O'Malley") as president of the [Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_the_Protection_of_Minors "Pontifical Commission for the Protection of Minors"). O'Malley endorsed the selection, describing Verny as "a collaborative leader committed to advancing the global adoption of protection and safeguarding, to as best possible assure the safety of those in the care of the Church throughout the world."[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-McElwee_PCPM_2025-183) On July 6, Leo revived the papal practice of taking summer residence at the [Castel Gandolfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Castel_Gandolfo "Palace of Castel Gandolfo"), which Francis had discontinued.[\[174\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-184)

On September 7, 2025, Leo presided over the canonization of [Carlo Acutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Acutis "Carlo Acutis") and [Pier Giorgio Frassati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pier_Giorgio_Frassati "Pier Giorgio Frassati") at a mass in [Saint Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_Square "Saint Peter's Square").[\[175\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-185) A month later, his first [Apostolic journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_journey "Apostolic journey"), a [visit to Turkey and Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visit_by_Pope_Leo_XIV_to_Turkey_and_Lebanon "Visit by Pope Leo XIV to Turkey and Lebanon"), was announced for November 27 through December 2.[\[176\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-186) On November 21, 2025, Leo signed an amendment to the 2023 law allowing women to become president of the [Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_the_Vatican_City_State "Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State"), removing a requirement that would-be officeholders must hold the rank of [cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)").[\[177\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-187) On November 27, 2025, Leo made his [first overseas visit as pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visit_by_Pope_Leo_XIV_to_Turkey_and_Lebanon "Visit by Pope Leo XIV to Turkey and Lebanon"), arriving in Turkey to commemorate the 1,700th anniversary of the [Council of Nicaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Council_of_Nicaea "First Council of Nicaea") with [Patriarch Bartholomew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartholomew_I_of_Constantinople "Bartholomew I of Constantinople") of the [Eastern Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church");[\[178\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-188)[\[179\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-189) while in Istanbul, he visited [the Blue Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Mosque,_Istanbul "Blue Mosque, Istanbul").[\[180\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-190)[\[181\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-191) Leo later visited Lebanon, visiting and praying at the site of the [2020 Beirut explosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Beirut_explosion "2020 Beirut explosion")[\[182\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-:0-192) and later the tomb of [Charbel Makhlouf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charbel_Makhlouf "Charbel Makhlouf")[\[183\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-193) before returning to Rome on December 2.[\[182\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-:0-192)

Views
-----

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Papa_Leone_XIII_%281898%29.jpg/250px-Papa_Leone_XIII_%281898%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Papa_Leone_XIII_/(1898/).jpg)

Prevost chose the papal name Leo in honor of [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII")'s social teachings.

Prevost's [regnal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") name was chosen in honor of [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII") (r. 1878–1903),[\[184\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-194) whose encyclical _[Rerum novarum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rerum_novarum "Rerum novarum")_ established modern [Catholic social teaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_social_teaching "Catholic social teaching") and promoted [labor rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_rights "Labor rights").[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Galeazzi_2025-145)[\[185\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-195) According to the [Holy See Press Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See_Press_Office "Holy See Press Office") director [Matteo Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Bruni "Matteo Bruni"), this choice is "clearly a reference to the lives of men and women, to their work – even in an age marked by artificial intelligence".[\[186\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-196) Leo XIV confirmed the association with Leo XIII in an address to the [World Meeting of Popular Movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_movement "Popular movement") in October 2025.[\[187\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-197)

According to Cardinal [Fernando Chomalí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Chomal%C3%AD "Fernando Chomalí") of Chile, Leo told him that the choice of papal name is based on his concern about the world's cultural shifts, a type of [Copernican Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copernican_Revolution "Copernican Revolution") involving [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") and [robotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics "Robotics"). Chomalí said: "He was inspired by [Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII"), who amid the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution") wrote _Rerum novarum_ launching an important dialogue between the church and the modern world."[\[188\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-198) Leo himself explained that "the church offers to everyone the treasury of her social teaching in response to [another industrial revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Industrial_Revolution "Fourth Industrial Revolution") and to developments in the field of artificial intelligence that pose new challenges for the defense of human dignity, justice, and labor."[\[189\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Kent_2025-199)[\[190\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Winfield_2025-200)[\[191\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-201)

In a May 2023 interview, Prevost stressed the need for prudence and responsibility on using social media to preclude "fueling divisions and controversy" and doing "damage to the communion of the Church".[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) This view is in line with his tendency to speak "with caution and great deliberation", as Christopher White, the Vatican correspondent of the _[National Catholic Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Catholic_Reporter "National Catholic Reporter")_, described him.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-White_2025-203)

The _National Catholic Reporter_ stated that Leo XIV is committed to [ecumenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenism "Ecumenism") with other [Christian denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denomination "Christian denomination").[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Reese2025-204) At [his inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV"), he referenced "sister Christian churches" and prayed for "a united church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world".[\[195\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Collins2025-205)[\[196\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-WCC2025-206)[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Gomes2025-61) Leo XIV's first international trip as pontiff was to [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") in November 2025, to celebrate the 1,700th anniversary of the [First Council of Nicaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Council_of_Nicaea "First Council of Nicaea") with other Christians.[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Reese2025-204)

Prevost has said religious freedom is "not optional but essential". During an audience with pontifical charity [Aid to the Church in Need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aid_to_the_Church_in_Need "Aid to the Church in Need"), before the launch of its Religious Freedom in the World Report in October 2025, Leo said that the right to religious freedom is "a cornerstone of any just society, for it safeguards the moral space in which conscience may be formed and exercised", adding that "religious freedom, therefore, is not merely a legal right or a privilege granted to us by governments; it is a foundational condition that makes authentic reconciliation possible."[\[197\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-207)

### Church policy

The new pope's first message emphasized the greeting of peace of the risen Jesus "who gave his life for God's flock", giving "an unarmed and disarming peace".[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208) Leo said he wanted to continue the [kerygmatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerygma "Kerygma") blessing of Pope Francis: "God cares for you, God loves you all, and evil will not prevail! We are all in God's hands."[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208) The themes in his first message included Jesus as [light needed by the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_of_the_World "Light of the World"), becoming a missionary church through dialogue and openness, fidelity to the [Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel "Gospel"), walking together in synodality, working as a united church for peace and justice, closeness to the suffering, and [praying to Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veneration_of_Mary_in_the_Catholic_Church "Veneration of Mary in the Catholic Church"). Twice he mentioned the need of not having fear, and emphasized God's help to "build bridges" for "all of us to be one people always in peace."[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208)

In his first address as Pope to the cardinals, Leo declared his "complete commitment" to the ecclesial path traced by the [Second Vatican Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council"). He praised Pope Francis's specification of this path through _[Evangelii Gaudium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelii_Gaudium "Evangelii Gaudium")_, the Joy of the Gospel, and highlighted six "evangelical principles", which he deems as perennial and revelatory of [God's mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divine_mercy "Divine mercy"): the [primacy of Christ in proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerygma "Kerygma"); the [missionary conversion of the entire Christian community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_evangelization "New evangelization"); [collegiality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collegiality_in_the_Catholic_Church "Collegiality in the Catholic Church") and synodality; attention to the _[sensus fidei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensus_fidei "Sensus fidei")_, the capacity of the whole faithful to sense the faith, especially [popular piety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_piety "Popular piety"); loving care for the least and the rejected; and dialogue with the contemporary world.[\[199\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-209)[\[200\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-210)

Leo XIV's episcopal motto is _In illo Uno unum_ ("In the One, we are one").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) On the official start of his pontificate, during the [inaugural Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV"), he requested that "our first great desire be for a united Church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world."[\[201\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-211) Noting that there is "too much discord" in the world, he stressed that "the two dimensions of the mission" of the papacy is "love and unity", as its authority is "a question of loving as Jesus did."[\[202\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-212)[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-213)

Discussing the [ordination of women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordination_of_women "Ordination of women") in October 2023, Prevost stated that the "very significant and long tradition of the church" makes it impossible to consider women as priests and that "the apostolic tradition is something that has been spelled out very clearly." By contrast, he observed that the possibility of women deacons has been the subject of two Vatican commissions, demonstrating "openness to giving consideration" to that question. He also cautioned that the ordination of women as deacons "doesn't necessarily solve a problem" and could create new issues.[\[204\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-214)[\[205\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Mares_2023-215)[\[206\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Zagano-2025-216) Commenting on Pope Francis's 2023 appointment of three women as members of the Dicastery for Bishops, which he headed, he noted that their perspectives often align with other members but can introduce new valuable viewpoints.[\[207\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-217)

As a cardinal, Prevost was a vocal proponent of [synodality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synodality "Synodality"), one of Pope Francis's signature initiatives. Prevost suggested that the participation and co-responsibility of all the faithful could address the polarization in the church.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-White_2025-203) In May 2023, Prevost said that [episcopal leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_leadership "Episcopal leadership") should prioritize faith over administration. The first priority is to "communicate the beauty of the faith, the beauty and joy of knowing Jesus."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) Also in May 2023, Prevost said he has faith that "the Holy Spirit is \[...\] pushing us towards a renewal."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) He stated that all the faithful are "called to the great responsibility of living what I call a new attitude," which is "to listen first of all to the Holy Spirit, to what He is asking of the Church."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202)

### Liturgical and ceremonial practice

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg/250px-Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV presiding over his inaugural papal Mass

During his service in [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"), Prevost was described as an "impeccable dresser" when it came to celebrating the Mass, wearing full vestments even when summer temperatures rose above 85 °F (about 29 °C) in Chiclayo.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Rich,_Dias_&_Horowitz_2025-64)[\[208\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-218)[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91) Prevost described himself as "very obedient" in liturgical matters, and urged that the liturgy be prepared "in the best way possible."[\[209\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-219) In August 2024, speaking to a Chicago-area parish, Prevost stated that "liturgy needs to be beautiful to help us, to strengthen us in our faith."[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-220) In his first Mass in the [Sistine Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel") as pope, he chose to use a [papal ferula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_ferula "Papal ferula"), or ceremonial staff, made for [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict XVI") and seldom used by Francis.[\[211\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-221)[\[212\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-222) The mozzetta worn after his election, and Benedict's ferula signaled to some a "return to normal" in the Holy See following the Francis papacy.[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-223)[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-224) However, during his Inauguration Mass in St Peter's Square on May 18, 2025, Leo XIV used the ferula of Pope Paul VI which is most commonly associated with Pope John Paul II, and frequently used by Francis.[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-225)[\[216\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-226)[\[217\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-227)[\[218\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-228) Pope Leo XIV received another pectoral cross upon his election, which he has been wearing instead of the one he wore during the conclave and his first appearance as pope. This one is silver, with relics of St. [Leo the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_I "Pope Leo I"), St. Augustine, St. [Thomas of Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_of_Villanova "Thomas of Villanova"), and Blessed [Anselmo Polanco Fontecha](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anselmo_Polanco "es:Anselmo Polanco").[\[219\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-229) He also chose to restore the custom of the Pope himself giving archbishops the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium"), which had been altered by Francis in 2015.[\[220\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-230)[\[221\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-231) In September 2025, it was announced that Leo had given permission for the [Tridentine Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tridentine_Mass "Tridentine Mass") to be said in St. Peter's Basilica the following month, the first time such permission had been granted since the promulgation of [Traditionis custodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditionis_custodes "Traditionis custodes") in 2021.[\[222\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-232)[\[223\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-233)

### Social and political issues

#### Overview

Within the context of church politics and theology, Prevost has been seen as a moderate or centrist, neither liberal nor conservative.[\[224\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-234) In April 2025, the Italian newspaper _[la Repubblica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Repubblica "La Repubblica")_ stated that Prevost was seen as a "cosmopolitan and shy figure" who was "appreciated by conservatives and progressives" within the church.[\[225\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-235)[\[k\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-237) In line with the church's official positions, Leo opposes [abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_abortion "Catholic Church and abortion"), [euthanasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_views_on_euthanasia "Catholic views on euthanasia"), [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_same-sex_marriage "Catholic Church and same-sex marriage") and the [death penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_capital_punishment "Catholic Church and capital punishment").[\[227\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-238)

#### Pro-life issues

Leo has [opposed abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-abortion "Anti-abortion") prior to and during his pontificate.[\[228\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-239) In 2012 stated that "[Western mass media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_mass_media "Western mass media") is extraordinarily effective in fostering within the general public enormous sympathy for beliefs and practices that are at odds with the Gospel—for example abortion, homosexual lifestyle, euthanasia". He reposted articles from the [Catholic News Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_News_Agency "Catholic News Agency"), including one from [Mike Pence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pence "Mike Pence") that was titled "Pence to pro-lifers: Win hearts with [compassion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compassion "Compassion") and love."[\[229\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-240)

Leo has opposed euthanasia[\[230\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-241) He expressed caution against the [euthanasia policy in Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euthanasia_in_Canada "Euthanasia in Canada"). He said that euthanasia, along with abortion, "discard the weakest", and disregard the [value of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_life "Right to life"). He has also stated "We cannot build a just society if we discard the weakest—whether the child in the womb or [the elderly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elder_rights "Elder rights") in their frailty—for they are both gifts from God."[\[231\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-242)

Prevost referred to opposition to the death penalty as [pro-life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-life "Pro-life").[\[232\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-243). This comment drew backlash, including from [conservatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatives "Conservatives") such as [Matt Walsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Walsh_/(political_commentator/) "Matt Walsh (political commentator)"), a [political commentator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_commentator "Political commentator"), who said it was "a terrible answer".[\[233\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-244)

#### LGBTQ+ issues

Prevost expressed reservations about "sympathy for beliefs and practices that contradict the gospel" and did not fully endorse or reject _[Fiducia supplicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiducia_supplicans "Fiducia supplicans")_, a declaration concerning blessings for people in a [same-sex relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_relationship "Same-sex relationship"). He stated that national bishops' conferences should "interpret and apply such directives in their local contexts, given cultural differences."[\[234\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-245) [Víctor Manuel Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_Manuel_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Víctor Manuel Fernández"), the head of the Vatican doctrine office, told _[Il Messaggero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_Messaggero "Il Messaggero")_ in July 2025 that he thought the blessing of those in same-sex unions, which had been approved under Pope Francis, would continue under Pope Leo. In May 2025, Cardinal [Jean-Claude Hollerich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Claude_Hollerich "Jean-Claude Hollerich") told _[La Stampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Stampa "La Stampa")_ that he believed Leo "might re-interpret" _Fiducia Supplicans,_ but not "abolish" it.[\[235\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-246)[\[236\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-247)

In 2012, Prevost criticized popular culture's sympathy for the "homosexual lifestyle" and same-sex families.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Rich_2025-142) In April 2016, he opposed the inclusion of "[gender ideology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_ideology "Gender ideology")" in Peruvian primary school curricula,[\[237\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-248) stating it promotes "genders that don't exist".[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Rich_2025-142) When asked in 2023 by [Catholic News Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_News_Service "Catholic News Service") whether his views from 2012 had changed, Prevost said that "many things have changed" and emphasized the church should be more open and welcoming though he cautioned that church doctrine has not changed.[\[238\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-249)[\[239\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-250)

In May 2025, Leo XIV said that it was up to governments to build peaceful societies "above all by investing in the family, founded upon the stable union between a man and a woman."[\[240\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-251) In September 2025, Leo told Reverend [James J. Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_J._Martin_/(priest/) "James J. Martin (priest)"), a major advocate for greater LGBTQ+ inclusion in the Church, that he would continue Francis' legacy of welcoming LGBTQ+ people into the Church, with Martin telling [The Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Associated_Press "The Associated Press") that their discussion "was very consoling and very encouraging and frankly a lot of fun."[\[241\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-252)

#### Geopolitics

[![Image 14](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Lula_Papa_Le%C3%A3o_XIV_13.10.2025_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Lula_Papa_Le%C3%A3o_XIV_13.10.2025_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lula_Papa_Le%C3%A3o_XIV_13.10.2025_/(cropped/).jpg)

Leo with President of Brazil [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva") in October 2025

During his time in Chiclayo, Prevost remained relatively politically neutral on national issues. However, in the midst of the [Peruvian protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_protests_/(2022%E2%80%932023/) "Peruvian protests (2022–2023)") in 2023, he stated: "The deaths during the protests cause me great sadness and pain \[...\] I asked to stay in Peru; I even made that request to the Holy Father. It wasn't the time to leave."[\[242\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-253) He has also expressed support for the plight of Venezuelan refugees in Peru.[\[243\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-McElwee_2025-254)[\[244\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-255) With regards to [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"), Prevost has advocated for stronger church action, stating in a November 2024 seminar that "dominion over nature" should not be "tyrannical".[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Burga_2025-157) He called for [Environmental protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_protection "Environmental protection"), supporting the installation of [solar panels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_panels "Solar panels") and [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicles "Electric vehicles").[\[245\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-256)

On geopolitics, Prevost has consistently advocated against armed conflict. He denounced the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), describing it as "a true invasion, imperialist in nature, where Russia seeks to conquer territory for reasons of power",[\[246\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-257) and in one of his first major speeches as pope, Leo called for a ceasefire in the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war"),[\[247\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-258)[\[248\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-259)[\[249\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-260) later describing Trump's then-proposed [Gaza peace plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_peace_plan "Gaza peace plan") as "realistic."[\[250\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Faiola_&_Craw_October_2025-261) Following the [Israeli strikes on Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_2025_Israeli_strikes_on_Iran "June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran") in June 2025, he urged Iranian and Israeli authorities to act with "reason".[\[251\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-262) On August 27, Leo said, "I beg for a permanent ceasefire to be reached, the safe entry of humanitarian aid to be facilitated and humanitarian law to be fully respected."[\[252\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-NBC,_Israel_faces_new_pressure_over_hospital_strikes,_August_27,_2025-263) [_The_ _Washington Post_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post") reported in September 2025 that Leo said the Vatican "at this time" cannot define the war as a "genocide", but he also noted that more and more people have described it as such.[\[253\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-264) Leo also issued prayers for those affected by the [clashes in southern Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Syria_clashes_/(July_2025%E2%80%93present/) "Southern Syria clashes (July 2025–present)") and the [2025 Cambodia–Thailand clashes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cambodia%E2%80%93Thailand_clashes "2025 Cambodia–Thailand clashes").[\[254\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-265) Leo lamented the [El Fasher massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Fasher_massacre "El Fasher massacre") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") during his Sunday Angelus address on November 2, 2025, calling for a ceasefire and humanitarian aid.[\[255\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-266) In November 2025, Leo criticized the [United States' military strikes against alleged drug traffickers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_military_strikes_on_alleged_drug_traffickers "2025 United States military strikes on alleged drug traffickers") near [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela"), warning that they were "increasing tension" and calling for diplomatic dialogue between the two countries.[\[256\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-AP_11-05-2025-267)

In his [Pentecost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecost "Pentecost") homily soon after his election as Pope, Leo criticized the "exclusionary mindset" displayed by various [nationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalism "Nationalism") movements. The [Holy Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_in_Christianity "Holy Spirit in Christianity") "breaks down barriers and tears down the walls of indifference and hatred", he said.[\[257\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Reuters1-268) To Leo, areas advertised as "security zones" had the effect of "separating us from our neighbors" and spreading "prejudice". He proclaimed that the Church needed to "open the borders between peoples and break down the barriers between class and race."[\[257\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Reuters1-268) Leo additionally condemned [femicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femicide "Femicide") during the homily, calling it both painful and tragic and attributing it to "an unhealthy desire for domination."[\[258\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Korea_Herald_2025-269)[\[259\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Allen_2025-270)

#### US politics

Throughout his time as a bishop and as a cardinal, Prevost continued to vote in both state and federal elections in the United States, being a [registered voter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_registration "Voter registration") in [Will County, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois "Will County, Illinois"). Illinois election law does not require voters to register affiliation with a political party, and Prevost has never officially done so.[\[260\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-271) The elections Prevost has voted in include the [2008 Democratic presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Illinois_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Illinois Democratic presidential primary"), the Democratic primary for the [2010 Illinois gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Illinois_gubernatorial_election#Democratic_primary "2010 Illinois gubernatorial election"), the [2012 Republican presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Illinois_Republican_presidential_primary "2012 Illinois Republican presidential primary"), the Republican primary for the [2014 Illinois gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Illinois_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2014 Illinois gubernatorial election"), the [2016 Republican presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Illinois_Republican_presidential_primary "2016 Illinois Republican presidential primary"), and the [2024 United States general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Illinois_elections "2024 Illinois elections").[\[261\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-272)[\[262\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-273)[\[263\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-274)

On the social media platform X (formerly [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter")), Prevost's former account reposted posts critical of US immigration policies under President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance").[\[264\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-275) He has also expressed support for [COVID-19 vaccination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination "COVID-19 vaccination") during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and sympathy for [George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd "George Floyd") and [protesters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-kim-25) His X account which he used prior to his election as Pope has since been deleted and he is currently using the official @Pontifex handle, inherited from Popes Benedict XVI and Francis.[\[265\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-276) As Pope, Leo avoided discussing US politics for the first few months of his pontificate, but in September 2025 reiterated past criticisms of the second Trump administration, remarking to a group of journalists that "someone who says 'I am against abortion but I am in agreement with the inhuman treatment of immigrants in the United States,' I don't know if that's pro-life."[\[266\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-McElwee_Trump_Leo_September_2025-277)[\[250\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Faiola_&_Craw_October_2025-261) White House press secretary [Karoline Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karoline_Leavitt "Karoline Leavitt") denied Leo's claims of maltreatment.[\[267\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Sentner_2025-278) That October, Leo urged labor unions in his home city of Chicago to fight for immigrants' rights. In November, he called for a "deep reflection" about American immigration policy and asked that detainees' "spiritual rights" be upheld via access to clergy.[\[256\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-AP_11-05-2025-267)

Personal life
-------------

In addition to his native English, Leo speaks Spanish, Italian, French, and Portuguese, as well as some German. He can also read Latin.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-NCR_2025-121)[\[268\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-279)[\[269\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-280) During his time in Peru, Leo learned a little of one of the [Quechuan languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuan_languages "Quechuan languages").[\[270\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-281)[\[271\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-282) He has described himself as "quite the amateur tennis player".[\[272\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-283) He is the first Pope who writes his own emails and wears a smartwatch, specifically an [Apple Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Watch "Apple Watch").[\[273\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Lamb-284) He regularly plays _[Wordle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordle "Wordle")_ and _[Words with Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Words_with_Friends "Words with Friends")_ with his brothers.[\[274\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-285)[\[275\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-286)

Leo is a lifelong fan of the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox") of [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball"),[\[276\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-287)[\[277\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-288)[\[278\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-289) and was in attendance at [US Cellular Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cellular_Field "US Cellular Field") for Game 1 of the [2005 World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Series "2005 World Series").[\[279\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-290)[\[280\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-291)[\[281\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-292) His support for [Chicago sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_in_Chicago "Sports in Chicago") also extends to the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League")'s [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"); United States Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") presented him with a custom Bears jersey following his papal inauguration, which Leo remarked was a "good choice".[\[282\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-293) He has also shown support for [Villanova University athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University_athletics "Villanova University athletics"), especially the [Villanova Wildcats men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_Wildcats_men%27s_basketball "Villanova Wildcats men's basketball") team.[\[283\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-294) In a review of an upcoming biography about him, the _Washington Post_ reported that in a hypothetical [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") match-up between the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men%27s_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team") and [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru_national_football_team "Peru national football team"), Leo would support Peru.[\[284\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-295)

As a teenager, he enjoyed driving recreationally.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Tucker_2025-44) Throughout his life, he has frequently preferred [driving long distances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_trip "Road trip") for journeys where most people would prefer to fly, such as from Philadelphia to Chicago, Brisbane to Sydney, and Chiclayo to Lima.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) He also repaired cars himself as a bishop in Chiclayo.[\[285\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-296)

For two years before becoming pope, Prevost, aged 68–69, would go two to three times a week to a gym for an hour, with a workout plan designed for men aged 50–55, focusing on posture and cardiovascular health. His personal trainer recalled Prevost's stamina and his being "always positive about everything".[\[286\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-297)

During his time as bishop of Chiclayo, aside from daily [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucharist "Eucharist") celebrated at 8 p.m. to ensure a clear mind, Prevost had [periods of prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_prayer "Mental prayer") at the beginning of the day and before dinner. He prayed [lauds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauds "Lauds") in the morning at the Cathedral and the [rosary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosary "Rosary") with his priest colleagues around noon.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91)

Honors
------

Villanova awarded him an honorary [Doctor of Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Humanities "Doctor of Humanities") degree in 2014.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-Mervosh_2025-53) In 2025, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_/(magazine/) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine included Leo among [the world's 100 most influential people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in [Artificial Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence "Artificial Intelligence").[\[287\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-298) On October 23, 2025, King [Charles III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III "Charles III") appointed Leo an Honorary Knight Grand Cross of the [Order of the Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Bath "Order of the Bath") on the occasion of the King's [state visit to the Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_visit_by_Charles_III_to_the_Holy_See "State visit by Charles III to the Holy See").[\[288\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-299) At the same event Leo accepted the title of _Papal Confrater of St. George's Chapel_ in Windsor Castle.[\[289\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Robert_Prevost#cite_note-300)

Biography of Robert Francis Prevost, Pope Leo XIV
=================================================

*   _._ 9 May 2025

![Image 6](https://cathnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/0509prev-Pope-Francis-gives-the-red-biretta-to-new-Cardinal-Robert-Prevost-during-a-consistory-in-St-Peter-s-Square-at-the-Vatican-in-this-file-photo-from-September-30-2023-CNS-Lola-Gomez.jpg)

![Image 7](https://cathnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/0509prev-Pope-Francis-gives-the-red-biretta-to-new-Cardinal-Robert-Prevost-during-a-consistory-in-St-Peter-s-Square-at-the-Vatican-in-this-file-photo-from-September-30-2023-CNS-Lola-Gomez.jpg)

Pope Francis gives the red biretta to then-Cardinal Robert Prevost during a consistory in St Peter’s Square at the Vatican in September 2023 (CNS/Lola Gomez)

Pope Leo XIV is the first Augustinian pope and the second Roman pontiff – after Pope Francis – from the Americas. Source: _Vatican News._

Unlike Jorge Mario Bergoglio, however, the 69-year-old Robert Francis Prevost is from the northern part of the continent, though he spent many years as a missionary in Peru before being elected head of the Augustinians for two consecutive terms.

He was born on September 14, 1955, in Chicago, Illinois, to Louis Marius Prevost, of French and Italian descent, and Mildred Martínez, of Spanish descent. He has two brothers, Louis Martín and John Joseph.

He spent his childhood and adolescence with his family and studied first at the Minor Seminary of the Augustinian Fathers and then at Villanova University in Pennsylvania, where in 1977 he earned a Degree in Mathematics and also studied Philosophy.

On September 1 of the same year, he entered the novitiate of the Order of St Augustine in St Louis and made his first profession on September 2, 1978. On August 29, 1981, he made his solemn vows.

The future pontiff received his theological education at the Catholic Theological Union in Chicago. At the age of 27, he was sent by his superiors to Rome to study Canon Law at the Pontifical University of St Thomas Aquinas (Angelicum).

In Rome, he was ordained a priest on June 19, 1982, at the Augustinian College of St Monica. Prevost obtained his licentiate in 1984 and the following year, while preparing his doctoral thesis, was sent to the Augustinian mission in Chulucanas, Piura, Peru (1985–1986).

In 1988, he joined the mission in Trujillo, also in Peru, as director of the joint formation project for Augustinian candidates from the vicariates of Chulucanas, Iquitos, and Apurímac.

In 1999, he was elected Provincial Prior of the Augustinian Province of “Mother of Good Counsel” in Chicago, and two and a half years later, the ordinary General Chapter of the Order of St Augustine elected him as Prior General, confirming him in 2007 for a second term.

In October 2013, he returned to his Augustinian Province in Chicago until Pope Francis appointed him on November 3, 2014, as Apostolic Administrator of the Peruvian Diocese of Chiclayo. His episcopal ordination was on December 12, 2014. He was appointed Bishop of Chiclayo on September 26, 2015.

On January 30, 2023, the Pope called him to Rome as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and President of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America, promoting him to the rank of Archbishop. He was created a cardinal on September 30, 2023.

Rome CNN  — 

Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost [has made history](https://www.cnn.com/world/live-news/new-pope-conclave-day-two-05-08-25).

The newly elected pontiff, now known as Pope Leo XIV, is the first pope from the United States, and the new leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.

The 69-year-old from Chicago stepped into his role as the 267th pope on the balcony of St. Peter’s Basilica on Thursday evening, addressing thousands of cheering Catholics with the words: “Peace be with you all.”

As he addressed the crowds in St. Peter’s Square, Leo paid tribute to the late pontiff Francis, urging them to remember the late pope’s legacy of unity before outlining his own vision for the Catholic Church.

“We have to seek together to be a missionary church. A church that builds bridges and dialogue,” he said. Speaking in Italian, Leo called on people to “show our charity” to others “and be in dialogue with love.”

[![Image 20: Cardinal Robert Prevost appears on the central loggia of St. Peter's Basilica after being chosen the 267th pontiff of the Roman Catholic Church, choosing the name of Pope Leo XIV, at the Vatican, Thursday, May 8, 2025. (AP Photo/Alessandra Tarantino)](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/05-ap25128631820628.JPG?c=16x9&q=h_144,w_256,c_fill) Cardinal Robert Prevost appears on the central loggia of St. Peter's Basilica after being chosen the 267th pontiff of the Roman Catholic Church, choosing the name of Pope Leo XIV, at the Vatican, Thursday, May 8, 2025. (AP Photo/Alessandra Tarantino) Alessandra Tarantino/AP video Related video Hear first American pope address the world](https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/08/world/video/new-pope-robert-prevost-leo-xiv-speech-digvid)

Leo was chosen just two days after a group of 133 cardinals gathered in conclave to select a new pontiff, ﻿suggesting that he quickly impressed his peers during the secretive process. He is expected to build on Francis’ reforms.

His predecessors, Francis and Benedict XVI, were both revealed in the evening of the conclave’s second day, while John Paul II, the longest-reigning pope of modern times, was selected on the third day, in 1978.

The coming days are for celebration; Leo’s name will be uttered in homilies and Masses across the Roman Catholic world, and will spark particularly joyous scenes in his home country, where one in five adults identifies as Catholic.

But leading the largest Christian denomination through an unpredictable era will require difficult and consequential decisions.

The new pope inherits a church whose image and ambitions were transformed by its predecessor; Francis pulled the priorities of the church away from social issues such as abortion, homosexuality, gender roles and contraception, advocating instead for the world’s poor, displaced and needy, and instilling a mission anchored in altruism.

And he must deal with crises from within, too. Francis’ [failure to bring a close](https://www.cnn.com/2025/04/24/europe/pope-clerical-sexual-abuse-scandal-reforms-intl-cmd/index.html) to the years-long scandal of child sexual abuse in the church despite some important steps will also reverberate through his successor’s papacy.

How to continue that trajectory will be a defining choice for the new pontiff, who, in his first moments as the new pope, signaled respect for Francis’ legacy but perhaps also a desire to set his papacy apart. In a reversion to norms, he wore traditional papal robes, whereas Francis had stepped out onto the balcony in a simple white cassock.

![Image 21: Conclave Watch: An American Pope - Square](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/cnn/audio/podcast-episode/52f1dae2-2a91-11f0-be57-ef789c0587c1/square.jpg?c=1x1&q=h_256,w_256,c_fill)

We have a pope – and he’s an American! Cardinal Robert Prevost has been selected as the next pope, the first American pontiff in history. He will be known as Pope Leo XIV. We break down the significance of this unprecedented moment and what challenges the Catholic Church's new leader will face as he takes over.  Guest: Christopher Lamb, CNN Vatican Correspondent

‘An exceptional leader’
-----------------------

Considered a highly capable and accomplished leader, Prevost most recently headed the powerful Vatican office for new bishop appointments, the Dicastery for Bishops, assessing candidates and making recommendations to the late pope. Francis appointed Prevost to the position, indicating he saw the US cleric as an effective leader.

He also made him president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America, where Prevost had spent much of his earlier career as a missionary.

The new pontiff is a member of the Augustinian religious order and spent more than a decade as its prior general, giving him experience of heading an order spread across the world.

![Image 22: The newly ordained Rev. Robert Prevost shakes hands with Pope John Paul II in 1982.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/3833483bcff8b8b4123d40702ae290343f3375b6.jpg?q=w_1110,c_fill)

The newly ordained Rev. Robert Prevost shakes hands with Pope John Paul II in 1982.

From St. Mary of the Assumption Parish

He worked for a decade in Trujillo, Peru, and was later appointed bishop of Chiclayo, another Peruvian city, where he served from 2014 to 2023. In 2015, he also received Peruvian citizenship.

In his inaugural address as pope, Leo switched from speaking in Italian to Spanish – one of several European languages he speaks – to address his “beloved diocese” in Chiclayo.

Peruvian President Dina Boluarte mirrored that sentiment, calling his election a “historic moment for Peru and the world,” in a Thursday address.

“In our lands, he sowed hope, walked alongside the most needy, and shared the joys of our people. … He chose to be one of us, to live among us, and to carry in his heart the faith, culture and dreams of this nation,” Boluarte said.

In the United States, President Donald Trump called the news a “great honor” for America, adding he looks forward to meeting the new pope. Vice President JD Vance, who converted to Catholicism in 2019, said in a message on X: “I’m sure millions of American Catholics and other Christians will pray for his successful work leading the Church.”

[![Image 23: Newly elected Pope Leo XIV, Cardinal Robert Prevost of the United States appears on the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica, at the Vatican, May 8, 2025. REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane ](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/04-2025-05-08t175329z-761212760-rc2tdea6716i-rtrmadp-3-pope-succession-leo.JPG?c=16x9&q=h_144,w_256,c_fill) Newly elected Pope Leo XIV, Cardinal Robert Prevost of the United States appears on the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica, at the Vatican, May 8, 2025. REUTERS/Guglielmo Mangiapane Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Related article What’s in a name? The history of the papal name Leo](https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/08/europe/papal-leo-pope-cardinal-pontiff-intl)

While it is often said cardinal electors would always shy away from choosing a pope from the United States, because of America’s outsized global political influence, Prevost’s long experience in Peru may have mitigated those fears among the electors.

“He’s somebody that, even though he’s from the West, would be very attentive to the needs of a global church,” said Elise Allen, CNN’s Vatican analyst. “You’re talking about somebody who spent over half of his ecclesial career abroad as a missionary in Peru.”

Allen added that he’s seen as a talented leader in Vatican circles. “He’s seen as somebody who is calm and balanced, who is evenhanded, and who is very clear on what he thinks needs to be done … but he’s not overly forceful in trying to make that happen.”

![Image 24: The newly elected Pope Leo XIV appears before the crowds in St. Peter's Square, saying they must "seek together to be a missionary church. A church that builds bridges and dialogue."](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/08-2025-05-08t173545z-790655945-rc2tdea7pxwa-rtrmadp-3-pope-succession.JPG?q=w_1110,c_fill)

The newly elected Pope Leo XIV appears before the crowds in St. Peter's Square, saying they must "seek together to be a missionary church. A church that builds bridges and dialogue."

Stoyan Nenov/Reuters

Prevost earned his bachelor’s in mathematics from Villanova University in Pennsylvania and went on receive his diploma in theology from the Catholic Theological Union of Chicago.

He was later sent to Rome to study canon law at the Pontifical Saint Thomas Aquinas University and was ordained as a priest in June 1982. Later in his career, he taught canon law in the seminary in Trujillo, Peru.

In an interview with [Vatican News](https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2023-05/archbishop-prevost-the-bishop-is-a-pastor-not-a-manager.html) shortly after he became the leader of the Dicastery for Bishops, Prevost said: “I still consider myself a missionary. My vocation, like that of every Christian, is to be a missionary, to proclaim the Gospel wherever one is.”

Upcoming challenges
-------------------

Adding to festivities, and to the new pope’s diary commitments, is the fact that 2025 is a jubilee year for the church – a special celebration announced by Pope John Paul II 25 years ago, which sees a busy schedule of Vatican-organized events.

But the world is also watching to see whether he will follow in the Franciscan path.

Francis’ rejection of opulence and his softer tone on social issues was praised by some Western leaders, but there remains a faction in the church advocating for a stricter line on questions of sex, gender, marriage and migration.

Asked about the contributions of three women who were made members of the Dicastery for Bishops, Prevost told Vatican News: “I think their appointment is more than just a gesture on the part of the Pope to say that there are now women here, too. There is a real, genuine, and meaningful participation that they offer at our meetings when we discuss the dossiers of candidates.”

![Image 25: Faithful react as the newly elected Pope Leo XIV appears at the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica on Thursday.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/06-ap25128647758131.JPG?q=w_1110,c_fill)

Faithful react as the newly elected Pope Leo XIV appears at the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica on Thursday.

Emilio Morenatti/AP

He must also choose carefully when to intervene on the world stage. Francis became increasingly political in the final years of his papacy, making the case for the rights of migrants, urging a ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war and suggesting – to the ire of Kyiv – that Ukraine should wave [“the white flag”](https://www.cnn.com/2024/03/10/europe/ukraine-pope-negotiations-russia-intl) and make concessions to end Russia’s war in the country.

These ongoing conflicts, and the rise of populism and authoritarianism around the world, set a complicated context in which the new pope – himself an important figure in global diplomacy – will operate.

And how Leo will handle the clerical sex abuse scandals that have long plagued the Church could also define his papacy. Though Francis [spoke defensively about his record](https://www.cnn.com/2025/04/24/europe/pope-clerical-sexual-abuse-scandal-reforms-intl-cmd) on the matter, and took some important steps to tackle systemic issues involving abuse, the previous pope was accused by survivors’ groups of failing to hold accountable bishops and cardinals accused of covering up abuse.

Previously addressing the responsibility of combating clerical abuse, Prevost told Vatican News: “There are places where good work has already been done for years and the rules are being put into practice. At the same time, I believe that there is still much to learn.”

Last year, Francis’ commission for child protection said in its first report that parts of the church are still [failing to ensure](https://www.cnn.com/2024/10/29/europe/catholic-church-abuse-pope-francis-commission-intl) that abuse is properly reported, and raised concerns about a “lack of transparency” in how the Vatican handled cases.

_CNN’s Lauren Kent and Christopher Lamb reported from Rome, and Rob Picheta, Christian Edwards and Kara Fox reported from London. CNN’s Abel Alvarado and Elise Hammond contributed to this report._
